chapter: The Second Herd and its sidemen
title: Carlos Gastel brings back original players; the trumpet section
summary: Manager Carlos Gastel insisted on bringing back Harris and Chubby; they try to recall the trumpet section including Bernie Glow and Ernie Royal.

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel
story.community_name: Who played in the band: reciting personnel

blocks.x: So when did some of the other guys come back? Was it after --

It was after -- actually we were running into obstacle courses with bookings and so on. And one thing led to another and -- well, the late Carlos Gaselle took over the personal management of the band, and he was the one who was obsessed with the idea that he had to have two or three of the people back who were in the original band.
And when he asked me whom I thought I would like or
who I could get, at this point, that's when Bill Harris came back and Chubbie, and I guess everybody.
Ernie Royal had -- now we're going to get into the names again. This is that period for me, that --
No. No, we had like all legit players. I'll have to get this --
Oh, it's probably right in that Columbia Thundering Herds. We'll get it.
Which one? Well, there's a couple of sections. You have Stan Fishelson. Bernie Glow. Ernie Glow.
Ernie Glow actually was the lead player.
Shorty, Irv Markowitz, and Ernie Royal, yeah. That's quite a section.
Right. Ernie had already left the band then.

Uh-huh. This was Summer Sequence, yeah, "I Told Ya Ya" "I Love You, Now Get Out." That I remember because (inaudible) "Keen and Peachy," "The Goof and I," was the same time. "Geefin' Eye," and "I've Got News For You." Yeah.
